questions.stem: What is created around a wire when an electric current flows through it?
questions.explanation: When electric current flows through a wire, it creates a magnetic field around the wire. This is the magnetic effect of a current and is the basis for electromagnets.

questions.stem: Which of the following would NOT increase the strength of an electromagnet?

options.text: Increasing the number of turns of wire
Using a copper core instead of an iron core

questions.explanation: Copper is not a magnetic material, so using a copper core would not strengthen the electromagnet. The strength can be increased by adding more turns, increasing the current, or using a soft iron core which is easily magnetised.
